findings.justification: E7 shows long-term debt as of June 27, 2026 was $71.340 billion. Since $71.340 billion < $82.430 billion, this confirms that Apple's long-term debt was lower as of June 27, 2026 than a year earlier.

E9 is a derived metric showing long-term debt at June 27, 2026 was $71.340 billion compared to $82.430 billion at the comparison period, with a decrease of approximately 13.45%. This directly confirms the assertion that long-term debt was lower.

E17 shows the balance sheet with non-current term debt of $71,340 million as of June 27, 2026 compared to $78,328 million as of September 27, 2025. While this compares to fiscal year-end rather than the exact comparison date, combined with E7 and E8 which show the exact dates, this provides additional confirmation of the decrease in long-term debt.
